title: Mastering the Two-Pointer Technique
subtitle: Solve sorted array problems in O(N) time with O(1) space
summary: The Two-Pointer approach reduces brute-force O(N^2) pair searches to linear O(N) time by moving pointers inward or outward based on condition checks.
key_points: Opposite Direction: One pointer at start (left = 0), another at end (right = n - 1).
Condition: If sum < target -> left++; If sum > target -> right--; If sum == target -> match found!
Classic Applications: Pair Sum, Container With Most Water, 3Sum, Valid Palindrome.
interview_tip: Always check if the array is already sorted. If not, sorting takes O(N log N) - check if hashing (O(N) space) is better!
